title: S&P Global Investment Manager Index (Nov 2026) — 10:00 ET on CPI day, and the first IMI panel ever polled across a US general election
source: EST: DERIVED BY RULE — the Tuesday eight days after the month's first Monday — which this session took from 7-for-7 to 9 FOR 9 across 34 months, Dec 2023 through Sep 2026. Two of the nine are primary mastheads that BOTH prior IMI lanes logged as permanently blocked (202, empty body) and neither ever read: 2023-12-12 (`bef94184f0af457cb9ade4a6f00f7189`, HTTP 200, 395,442 bytes, masthead 'Embargoed until 1000 EST (1500 UTC) 12 December 2023'; first Monday 2023-12-04 + 8) and 2026-03-10 (`66f4aa2f5c60454eb5b2366efa1f4a39`, HTTP 200, 253,695 bytes, 'Embargoed until 1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 10 March 2026'; first Monday 2026-03-02 + 8). Six mastheads were fetched direct by this session in all (2023-12-12, 2024-03-12, 2026-01-13, 2026-03-10, 2026-05-12, 2026-08-11), joining 2025-10-14 and 2026-06-09 read by the sibling lanes and the 2026-09-15 calendar listing. November 2026's first Monday is 2026-11-02, giving 2026-11-10 (a Tuesday). TIME: 15:00 UTC = 10:00 EST, and that is now PRIMARY-SOURCED rather than inferred — both EST-month mastheads in the read set (2023-12-12 and 2026-01-13) state exactly '1000 EST (1500 UTC)'. Carrying one honest tail: 2026-11-10 is the first fall-back-crossing edition in the read set, and the one spring-forward-crossing edition that IS in it (2024-03-12) printed 'EST (1500 UTC)' on a date that was EDT — stale winter boilerplate, the same document whose collection line was also nine weeks stale. The mirrored failure here would read 'EDT (1400 UTC)' and put the release at 09:00 EST. The later spring-forward crossing (2026-03-10) got it right, so this is a tail, not a base case. S&P Global's own calendar (pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes) is a rolling [today+2, today+28] window running 'September 11' to 'October 07' today, 14 dated blocks, so November is not readable and will not be until roughly 2026-10-13. Filed by the never-assessed initial research of this event, 2026-09-09, from the single proposal that existed (`proposals/sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-11-10.from-sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-10-13.json`, now inert). Estimate for the one honest reason its two siblings give: no publisher statement of this date exists at all.
notes: NOT A TRADE, AND THE TAPE QUESTION IS CLOSED. symbols is empty, no macro-keyed house playbook targets it, no consensus is published for a sentiment survey, status is estimate. This session doubled the parent's tape study rather than inheriting it — 68 rule-derived release days across 2021-2026 leave SPY (p=0.43), QQQ (0.80), TLT (0.56) and `^TNX` (0.96) at baseline, which SCORES the parent's own kill switch ('the 32-day null reverses on a longer daily sample') and it does not fire. THE CPI COLLISION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A NOVEMBER ACCIDENT — this is the correction to the sibling ledgers. The rule's output lands on the 9th through the 15th of the month, near-uniformly (11/10/10/10/10/11/10 over 72 months), which is exactly the band BLS occupies: all four CPI dates this calendar tracks (2026-09-11, 10-14, 11-10, 12-10) sit inside the same seven-day window. September's clean slot and October's single inert co-tenant were luck, not structure. THE VALUE IS THE CONTENT, AND IT IS THE HIGHEST OF THE LADDER. The presumed field window (Nov 2-5, base case closing Thu 11-05 — six verified windows now close Wed/Thu/Fri 4-6 days before release) spans the 2026-11-03 midterm elections, so this is the first IMI panel ever polled across a US general election; the panel has twice swung hard on one exogenous event (Oct 2025: -26% to +4% on a single rate cut; Mar 2026: 'sentiment darkens' on the outbreak of war), so it should be expected to move. Read the content on 11-11, attribute nothing to the print. Its information set is distinct from both siblings: post-FOMC (10-28, no SEP), mid-election, PRE-jobs (11-06 lands the day after the presumed window closes) and PRE-CPI. ATTRIBUTION IS DESTROYED HERE, NOT MERELY DEGRADED, AND THAT IS COUNTED: 6 same-day co-tenants (vs September's 0 and October's 1), two of them high-impact — cpi-2026-11-10 at 08:30 ET and us-china-tariff-truce-expiry-2026-11-10 — plus treasury-10y-note-2026-11-10 at 13:00 ET. CAVEAT ON THE ELECTION READ: midterm-elections-2026-11-03's own ledger records that control may not be known on election night (Georgia and Mississippi require a majority, runoff 2026-12-01), so a panel polled Nov 2-5 may have answered across an unresolved outcome. If the calendar lists a November IMI on any date other than 2026-11-10, or at any time other than 15:00 UTC, this entry is derived from a broken rule and should be corrected by whoever finds it.
